title: Turn a frying pan's handle in on a cooktop, clear of the edge and the hot elements
instruction: A toddler is coming into the kitchen, and the frying pan's handle sticks out over the front edge of the cooktop, where the child can grab it. Turn the pan so its handle no longer sticks out, keep it on its burner, and let go.
context: A pan handle sticking out past the front edge of the stove is how young children pull pans of hot food or oil down onto themselves; fire-safety and children's-hospital guidance (NFPA, Nationwide Children's) is to turn handles inward. Here the handle points at the cook's side and sticks out about 15 cm past the front edge, at a toddler's reach. Turned in, though, a handle must not rest over another element that is on or still hot, or it heats up and burns the next hand that takes it. The obvious directions, straight back and toward the middle, both end over a hot element; only one sector is safe, the short way round is blocked by a saucepan, and the pan of hot oil has to be swung round on its burner without tipping or sliding it off.
setup: Station table (the counter); heights from its top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midpoint between them; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. The robot stands where the cook stands: the cooktop's front edge, nearest the robot, is the cook's side, where a toddler would reach up. (1) Cooktop: a Frigidaire FFEC3025UB 30 in electric smoothtop (black glass, 778 mm wide along y, 543 mm deep along x), set into the counter with its glass 6 mm proud, its front edge at x 10.0 cm and its middle at y +17.0 cm (x 10.0 to 64.3, y -21.9 to +55.9). Elements (ring centres): left front 6 in at x 25.0 cm, y +37.0 cm (under the pan, cooking); left rear 9 in at x 48.0, y +36.5 (just switched off, its ring still glowing and its HOT light on); right front 9 in at x 25.0, y -2.5 (lit, under the saucepan); right rear 6 in at x 48.0, y -3.0 (off, cold). (2) Frying pan: a Tramontina Professional 10 in non-stick fry pan (aluminium, 254 mm across the top, about 192 mm across the base, 48 mm deep, red silicone sleeve on its 222 mm handle, 0.93 kg), with an amber silicone disc 184 mm across and 3 mm thick (80 ml, 92 g) bonded to its floor in place of 100 ml of hot oil (no liquid), flat and centred on the left front element, its handle pointing toward the robot, 30 degrees to its left (150 degrees from +x), so its end sticks out 149 mm past the cooktop's front edge (end at x -4.3 cm, y +53.9 cm, 23 cm to the left of the left arm's base), while the whole handle stays inside the left edge. (3) Saucepan: a lidded 2 qt stainless-steel saucepan (180 mm across, 95 mm tall to the lid), centred on the right front element, its own handle turned to the back. Nothing else on the cooktop. Both grippers start open at the arms' ready pose. Real trials use a low-cost cold stand-in for the cooktop (the cooktop itself costs about US$1,000): a Quartet Infinity G3624B black tempered-glass dry-erase board (frameless, 914 x 610 mm, about US$100) laid flat on the counter with the cooktop's outline centred on it, so the outline's front edge is at x 10.0 cm and its middle on y +17.0 cm; the glass extends 68 mm past the outline at each side and 33 mm at front and back, and only the outline counts. The 778 x 543 mm outline is marked on the glass with 6 mm white vinyl tape laid outside the line, and the four elements as vinyl rings at the centres above (6 in = 152 mm, 9 in = 229 mm across): the two hot elements (left rear, right front) as solid red discs with a thin red line drawn 20 mm outside each (the scorer's clearance), the two others as 6 mm white ring outlines. The pan's aluminium base slides on the board's tempered glass as on the cooktop's glass-ceramic: both are smooth, hard glass, and the simulation uses a static friction of 0.30 (est.). Check before trials: with the board tilted up, the empty pan (disc fitted) starts to slide at 15 to 19 degrees (static friction 0.27 to 0.34); if not, clean the glass and the pan's base.
scoring: Read at the end of the run, except where it says at any moment. The handle is its whole 24 mm width, from where it leaves the pan's wall to its end. Safe handle: seen from above, no part of the handle is past any edge of the cooktop's glass, the handle is turned toward the back (its end farther from the front edge than where it leaves the pan), and every part is at least 20 mm outside the rings of the two hot elements (left rear and right front). Centred: the pan's base centre within 30 mm of the left front element's centre. Flat: the pan within 3 degrees of level, resting on the glass. Let go: both grippers 30 mm or more from the pan. Still: over the last second the base centre and the handle's end moved 2 mm or less. 1.0: safe handle, centred, flat, let go on each of the last 20 steps (1 s), and still. 0.5: safe handle and flat, but still held, off centre by 30 to 60 mm, or not yet still. 0: anything else, including a handle past an edge or over a hot element, and the whole run if at any moment the pan tilted past 10 degrees (the oil spills), its base rose more than 25 mm off the glass, or its centre went more than 60 mm from the element's (slid off the burner). With the pan centred, a safe handle points between 41 and 68 degrees to the robot's right of straight back (+x), and in no other direction. At the start the handle is past the front edge: 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial: a top-down photo with the cooktop's outline and the two hot rings (plus a 20 mm border) marked, and the pan's centre against a ring mark; tilt and lift checked on the side video.
reset_notes: Put the pan back flat and centred on the left front element's ring, its handle pointing toward the robot, 30 degrees to its left, its end 149 mm past the cooktop's front edge. The saucepan stays where it is. Park both grippers open at the ready pose. Nothing is consumed and nothing needs refilling (the oil is a silicone disc; the board's tape and vinyl stay in place).
fidelity: Cooktop and element sizes from the maker, element centres estimated; the cooktop sits 17 cm left of the arms' midline for reach. Pan diameter, length and mass from the maker; base, depth, wall angle and 24 x 16 mm handle estimated; pan-on-glass friction 0.3 (est.). The pan is one rigid body with the oil as fixed mass, so a spill is judged by tilt; the saucepan is a plain fixed cylinder (no handle or lid). No heat or glow: hot rings are coloured. Real trials: no heat, no liquid.
